title: Under the glare of a luminous quasar, the FIR continuum is still an excellent tracer of the ISM down to the central kiloparsec
question: Whether far-infrared continuum emission measured on galaxy-wide scales in luminous z=2 quasar hosts is primarily attributable to ongoing star formation or significantly enhanced by quasar-heated dust.

data.angular_resolution: Band 5: ~0.1 arcsec (high-res) and ~1 arcsec (low-res), combined ~0.2 arcsec; Band 9: 0.30-0.35 arcsec (J1236+0500) and 0.06x0.10 arcsec (J2345-1104); Band 7: 0.9 arcsec
data.sensitivity: J1236+0500 Band 5 CO rms = 0.08 Jy beam^-1 km s^-1; J1236+0500 Band 5 continuum rms = 0.029 mJy beam^-1

what.value: Initial Band 7 850 um continuum fluxes, luminosities, SFRs, black hole masses, and bolometric luminosities of the three quasars

evidence.quote: Initial estimates of their SFRs are measured using ALMA continuum observations in Band 7 (Cycle 5; 2017.1.00102.S; PI: A. Schulze) with a spatial resolution of 0.9$^{\prime\prime}$ (cite: Schulze2019).
Their basic properties from the Band 7 data are listed in Table [\[tab:sample\]](#tab:sample).

what.value: Compilation of star-forming galaxies and lower-luminosity AGNs at 1 < z < 1.7 with CO(5-4) and IR luminosity measurements

evidence.quote: Lastly, the dust and CO emission from these three quasar hosts will be compared with a compilation of star-forming galaxies and lower-luminosity AGNs at $1<z<1.7$ (cite: Valentino2021) to conclude on the quasar contribution to the total FIR emission.

evidence.loc: Discussion / Dynamical and inferred stellar masses
evidence.quote: For reference, we include the sample of quasars at $z\sim2$ from the (cite: Mechtley2016) study as a reference which generally cover the region of our three quasars.

recipe.goal: Coadd visibilities and fit two-component models (host + point source) in the uv-plane
recipe.method: Coadd high and low resolution Band 5 visibilities using CASA 'concat', export to GILDAS via 'exportuvfits' and 'fits.to.uvt', and perform two-component (elliptical Spergel profile + central point source) fitting in the uv-plane using 'uv_fit' for CO(5-4) and continuum (Bands 5, 7, 9).
key_parameters: CO velocity integration ranges (FWHM): 455 km s^-1 (J1236+0500), 220 km s^-1 (J2317-1033), 480 km s^-1 (J2345-1104)
Continuum Spergel index tested for 3 cases: fixed to CO fit value, fixed to -0.3, and free
assumptions: H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7
Point-source component traces unresolved quasar/torus emission while extended Spergel component traces the host galaxy

recipe.goal: Model 3D gas kinematics of SDSS J1236+0500
recipe.method: Fit the CO(5-4) data cube with a 3D tilted-ring thin disk model using 3D-Barolo and fit the 1D spectrum with a double Gaussian profile.

recipe.goal: Construct FIR SEDs, derive IR luminosities and SFRs, and evaluate the CO-FIR relation
recipe.method: Compare decomposed extended and nuclear fluxes across Bands 5, 7, and 9 with modified blackbody models and Lyu et al. (2017) quasar templates; compute L'_CO(5-4), convert to L_TIR via Daddi et al. (2015) and to SFR via Kennicutt & Evans (2012); fit empirical AGN contribution to CO(5-4) following Valentino et al. (2021).
key_parameters: Modified blackbody parameters: beta = 1.6, T_dust = 47 K
assumptions: Point-source emission originates from the unresolved quasar component while extended emission is heated solely by star formation

recipe.goal: Estimate host galaxy dynamical masses and CO Tully-Fisher stellar masses
recipe.method: Extract 1D CO(5-4) spectra within a 1 arcsec aperture for pixels with S/N > 2, fit double-horn (J1236+0500, J2345-1104) or single Gaussian (J2317-1033) line profiles, and compute M_dyn(R) using MCMC and M_* using the local CO Tully-Fisher relation.
key_parameters: Aperture diameter = 1 arcsec; pixel selection threshold S/N > 2
assumptions: Rotation-dominated thin disk with inclination cos(i) = b/a and circular velocity v_circ = 0.5 * W_20 / sin(i)

evidence.quote: The disk is rotation dominated with $v/\sigma=6.5$ ($v_{rot}=260$ km s$^{-1}$ and $\sigma=40$ km s$^{-1}$).

score_reason: All four ALMA project codes, CASA pipeline versions, and primary analysis packages (CASA, GILDAS uv_fit, 3D-Barolo) are explicitly stated alongside detailed tabular results, though exact channel masks, 3D-Barolo ring settings, and intermediate kinematic parameters (W20, W50, b/a) are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA project codes are explicitly identified, the core methodology (CASA concat + GILDAS uv_fit with a Spergel + point source model) is well-defined, and the main results (component fluxes, effective radii, CO luminosities, SFRs, and v/sigma) are numeric and tabulated in Table 2.
